title: NYU Stern course materials — Ratios, undated accessible lecture PDF
use: Brief primary-course orientation to diagnostic ratio families and numerator/denominator definitions. Chapter independently derives its identities and original examples under explicit conventions.
verification: Actual 18-page PDF inspected: printed Ratios1–2 (definitions, common-size and limitations), 5–8 (matched activity flows, liquidity, cash cycle), 12–16 (debt/coverage and three/five-factor ROE). The original source's date and individual author are not established from the accessible body. No source cases copied. Source statements suggesting that a low/high ratio identifies inefficiency or manipulation are narrowed to alternative hypotheses; ratios do not identify causes. This chapter does not reproduce a uniform threshold, use the historical lease formula as a current filing rule, or equate the equity multiplier with one plus interest-bearing debt/equity. Current inspection does not establish universal present-day reporting validity.

title: Aswath Damodaran — Return on Capital (ROC), Return on Invested Capital (ROIC) and Return on Equity (ROE): Measurement and Implications, July 2007
use: Scoped orientation to matching operating earnings and invested capital, cash exclusion, alternative timing conventions and accounting measurement/negative-equity limitations.
verification: Actual original-author faculty-hosted PDF inspected; title/date confirmed on printed page1 and scoped body on printed pages7–12, including book capital/cash adjustment, beginning versus average capital and negative book equity. Paper advocates beginning capital in its stated rationale and acknowledges average capital; our endpoint-average convention is explicitly our own choice. Used for stable methods only: no historical company figures, current sector averages, forecast persistence or general currency normalization recommendation is adopted. Original Aster derivations, numbers, policy comparison and code are not reproduced from the paper.

title: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission — Beginners' Guide to Financial Statement, 5 February 2007
use: Brief investor-education pointer to explanatory notes and management discussion as context for reported statements.
verification: Actual official HTML read, particularly notes, Read the MD&A and ratio sections; displayed last-reviewed date is 5 February2007. This is a dated educational guide, not a current accounting or disclosure rule. The guide's debt/equity paragraph mixes total debt and total liabilities; the chapter deliberately supplies its own interest-bearing-debt definition and distinguishes the liabilities-based measure. Its working-capital liquidation shorthand and owner-contribution interpretation are not used. No claim that the guide proves Aster's conventions are permitted in a real filing.
